# Tjo, in full

Version v0.11.0. Everything in llms.txt, plus the signatures and the worked
examples. If you are generating Tjo code, read the "what models get this wrong
about" section of llms.txt first: it is short and it is where the mistakes are.

## Starting a project

```bash
go install github.com/jimmitjoo/tjo/cmd/tjo@latest
tjo new myapp -t default -d postgres   # templates: default, blog, api, saas
cd myapp
tjo make auth                          # users, tokens, login, 2FA, remember-me
tjo migrate up
tjo run
```

`tjo make` is the way code enters a project. The templates live in
`cmd/tjo/templates/` and generated output is deterministic; hand-written
equivalents drift from the templates, which is how `tjo make auth` once came to
emit 181 references to a struct that no longer existed.

## Testing this repository

It is a workspace. From the root, `go test ./...` covers the root module only
and silently skips `email`, `otel`, `sms` and `websocket`. That blind spot
shipped six defects and 71 reachable vulnerabilities behind a green build.

```bash
make test   # all five modules
make vuln   # govulncheck, all five modules
```

## auth

Verbs and store interfaces. It never owns a table.

```go
// Login. The lookup and the bcrypt comparison happen unconditionally and in
// that order, so an unknown address costs the same as a known one.
account, err := auth.AuthenticateAndUpgrade(ctx, store, email, password,
    func(ctx context.Context, a auth.Account, newHash []byte) { /* store it */ })

// Password reset. Consumes the token atomically and returns the hash to write.
userID, hash, err := auth.ResetPassword(ctx, store, auth.DefaultPasswordPolicy(), token, newPassword)

// Two-factor. lastStep is replay protection and is not optional: store the
// returned step against the account and pass it back.
step, err := auth.VerifyTOTP(secret, code, time.Now(), user.TOTPLastStep)

// Recovery codes and remember-me are single-use tokens on the same store.
codes, err := auth.NewRecoveryCodes(ctx, store, userID, ttl)
token, err := auth.Remember(ctx, store, userID, auth.DefaultRememberTTL)
userID, replacement, err := auth.Recall(ctx, store, token, auth.DefaultRememberTTL)

// Passkeys. Both ceremonies; the credential is stored as one opaque string.
passkeys, err := auth.NewPasskeys(auth.PasskeyConfig{
    RelyingPartyID: "example.com", Origins: []string{"https://example.com"},
}, store)
ceremony, err := passkeys.BeginRegistration(ctx, accountID, name, displayName)
record, err := passkeys.FinishRegistration(ctx, accountID, label, ceremony.State, r)
```

Interfaces you implement: `auth.Account` (three methods), `auth.AccountStore`,
`auth.ResetStore`, `auth.PasskeyStore`, `auth.OrganizationStore`.
`auth.SQLResetStore` and `auth.SQLPasskeyStore` are provided because their
atomicity requirements are what a hand-written version gets wrong.

## admin

```go
panel := admin.New(admin.Config{DB: db, Driver: "postgres", Authorizer: rules})
panel.Register(admin.Resource{Model: User{}, Table: "users"})
mux.Handle("/admin/", http.StripPrefix("/admin", panel.Handler("/admin")))
```

Field types, labels and which columns are searchable come from the struct.
Override with an `admin:"..."` tag: `label=`, `hidden`, `show`, `readonly`,
`required`, `search`, `file`, `choices=a|b|c`, `belongsTo=table.key:label`.

Columns named like credentials (`password`, `token_hash`, `totp_secret`, ...)
are hidden unless the tag says `show`. There is no permissive authorizer
default: without one every request is answered 404.

## ops

```go
recorder := ops.NewRecorder(0)
provider.TracerProvider().RegisterSpanProcessor(recorder)

panel.AddPage(ops.Page(ops.Config{
    Recorder: recorder,
    Queues:   []*jobs.SQLQueue{queue},
    Health:   database.NewHealthChecker(db, 2*time.Second),
}))
```

## jobs

```go
queue := jobs.NewSQLQueue(db, "default", jobs.DialectPostgres)
queue.Migrate(ctx)
queue.PushTx(ctx, tx, job)   // enqueue inside the transaction that motivated it

// Durable steps. A step runs once; a replay returns the stored result.
workflows := jobs.NewWorkflows(db, jobs.DialectPostgres)
workflows.Migrate(ctx)

func handle(ctx context.Context, job *jobs.Job) error {
    wf := workflows.For(job)

    charge, err := jobs.Step(ctx, wf, "charge", chargeCard)
    if err != nil {
        return err          // including *jobs.Parked -- return it unchanged
    }
    if err := wf.Sleep(ctx, "settle", 24*time.Hour); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    return jobs.Do(ctx, wf, "receipt", func(ctx context.Context) error {
        return sendReceipt(charge)
    })
}
```

`Sleep` and `WaitForEvent` return `*jobs.Parked`. A handler that swallows it
tells the worker the job succeeded and the workflow is lost.

## sse

```go
stream, err := sse.New(w, r)
broker.Serve(stream, "invoices")     // returns on disconnect, unsubscribes itself

broker.Patch("invoices", "patch", "<li>INV-1042 paid</li>")   // from anywhere
```

Serve behind HTTP/2. Under HTTP/1.1 a browser caps an origin at six connections
and an SSE response never completes.

## database

```go
rows, err := database.NewQueryBuilder(db).WithDialect(database.DialectDollar).
    Table("invoices").
    Where("status", "=", "unpaid").
    OrderBy("created_at", "DESC").
    Paginate(1, 25).
    Get()
```

## Conventions in this codebase

- Comments explain why, not what. Several record a bug that a change prevents.
- Commit messages describe the defect and the evidence, not the diff.
- Prefer the standard library. v0.9.0 removed four dependencies by replacing
  them with stdlib calls or forty lines.
- Every fix ships a regression test that was run against the unfixed code and
  observed to fail.
